subject: Learning Methods
title: The Pomodoro Technique
description: A fast breakdown of The Pomodoro Technique for builders.

hook.text: Francesco Cirillo used a tomato-shaped kitchen timer in college. He set it for 25 minutes and changed how he worked.

buildup.text: Work for 25 minutes, break for 5. After four cycles, take a longer 15-minute break. Repeat all day.

discovery.text: The timer creates urgency. Knowing the break is coming makes starting easier. Small commitments beat vague intentions.

twist.text: Some tasks need unbroken 90-minute blocks. Pomodoro works best for tasks that require discipline to start, not deep.

climax.text: Use Pomodoro to overcome procrastination. Switch to longer blocks once momentum carries you forward naturally.

punchline.text: Twenty-five minutes. One tomato at a time.

quiz.question: When is the Pomodoro Technique most effective?
options: For tasks requiring deep creative thinking
For tasks that require discipline to start
